contract.name: Button
contract.summary: FinCore's action control: one text label, three visual variants and five mutually exclusive Figma states. Authored from the verified Figma Button set and the 195-token foundation. Implemented as framework-agnostic CSS with native HTML reference markup; no runtime package or adapter.
contract.maturity: implemented; framework-agnostic CSS + native HTML; no runtime package

evidence: Figma file llp3APU7qaknEGJWq7vTI4, page 1:3, Button set 87:37: Stage B verification PASS, 15 variants, 204/204 bindings. 22 unique button.* tokens; 0 primitive or Semantic bypasses. The former Ghost/Focus drift (label 87:34 bound to color/content/link) was corrected to button/ghost/foreground (VariableID:82:160) and verified in the Stage 5C-1 post-write inspection.
Repository token source tokens/tokens.json sha256 68caea55e0bdf9f5cda067d7993eee91ad6cc277a7aca81a19ec566bd33c6379: 195 foundation tokens, 95 primitive / 50 semantic / 50 component.
Stage C Input verification used the same foundation and preserved Button 87:37 unchanged: 15 variant IDs, 572x268 at (80,120), 3 properties.
tokens/check.mjs: structure PASS, required contrast pairs PASS, generated CSS current at contract authoring.

component: Render the supplied label using the variant and resolved interaction state.
Apply only button.* component tokens for colour, geometry and typography.
Expose a native disabled state that removes the control from interaction and tab order.
Render a visible focus indicator for keyboard focus and preserve it at every supported surface.
Provide native button semantics: activation with Enter and Space, focusability, and form submission when type is submit.
Remain presentational: it does not decide business rules, validate forms, navigate, or manage async work.
application: Choose the variant and write the label; only one primary action should lead a view or section.
Handle click and submit events, prevent duplicate submissions, and provide feedback outside the button when work is asynchronous.
Use a link, not Button, for navigation.
Use the native disabled attribute only when the action is genuinely unavailable, not as a substitute for validation or explanation.
Localise labels and allow them to grow without clipping.
Validate forms and move focus to the first invalid field; Button must not own validation.
Ensure a surrounding container does not clip the focus ring.
figmaOnly: State is a Figma VARIANT axis with five values; it is design metadata, not a runtime prop or an ARIA value.
Label is a Figma TEXT property with the demo default 'Button'; production copy is supplied by the application.
The Focus variant wraps a nested Surface frame in the ring frame; this is a Figma construction detail, not a DOM requirement.
Variant and State names are capitalised in Figma and lowercase in the production API mapping.

intended: The single strongest action in a form, dialog, panel or review step, for example 'Review transfer' or 'Save changes'.
A secondary, non-destructive alternative in the same decision group, for example 'Cancel' next to a primary action.
A low-emphasis action in a dense toolbar, row or navigation-adjacent area where a filled surface would add noise.
A disabled action when the action is genuinely unavailable and the reason is explained in surrounding content.
Form submission when the application needs native submit semantics and keyboard activation.

inappropriate.use: Navigating to another page, route or external site.
inappropriate.reason: Button is an action control; a button that changes location breaks expected browser and assistive-technology behaviour.
inappropriate.alternative: Use a semantic link with the same visual treatment supplied by the application, or a future Link component.

inappropriate.use: An icon-only action with no visible text.
inappropriate.reason: There is no icon system in v0.1 and no icon-only variant; an unlabelled icon would rely on an invented accessible-name pattern.
inappropriate.alternative: Use a text label. Wait for an icon and icon-button contract.

inappropriate.use: Showing loading, progress or a spinner.
inappropriate.reason: No loading state, spinner, progress token or async variant exists.
inappropriate.alternative: Keep the action's label stable and expose async status in a separate live region; disable or guard duplicate submission in the application.

inappropriate.use: Destructive or dangerous actions such as deleting an account.
inappropriate.reason: There is no danger, critical or destructive variant; a red override would break the token contract and contrast guarantees.
inappropriate.alternative: Do not implement destructive styling in v0.1. Raise a design-system request for a destructive variant.

inappropriate.use: A toggle, pressed state or segmented selection.
inappropriate.reason: No pressed, selected or toggle state exists and no aria-pressed contract is defined.
inappropriate.alternative: Use a future Toggle, Switch or Segmented Control component.

inappropriate.use: Two equally weighted primary actions for the same decision.
inappropriate.reason: Competing primary actions remove the visual hierarchy the variant exists to create.
inappropriate.alternative: Choose one primary action and use Secondary or Ghost for the alternative.

inappropriate.use: A Ghost button on an inverse or dark surface.
inappropriate.reason: Ghost text uses color.content.primary, which fails on color.surface.inverse (1.00:1); inverse surfaces are not supported in v0.1.
inappropriate.alternative: Use Primary or Secondary only after design review of the surface, or stay on a supported light surface.

inappropriate.use: A disabled button as the only explanation that a form is incomplete.
inappropriate.reason: A disabled control cannot receive focus or explain why it is unavailable, and it hides the validation message that would help the user proceed.
inappropriate.alternative: Keep the action enabled and validate on submit or blur, moving focus to the first invalid field.

structure: One text label inside one button surface. No icons, badges, counters or nested interactive elements.
Non-focus variants: the component frame is the button surface; it hugs the label horizontally and is 40px high.
Focus variants: the component frame is the focus ring, with a nested 'Surface' frame carrying the variant surface and label. The ring is drawn OUTSIDE the surface.
The label is a single line of text at 14/20, weight 500, IBM Plex Sans Medium in Figma.
Horizontal padding is 16px; vertical padding is 10px, derived from the 40px height and 20px line height.
The button is borderless. State is communicated by surface fill and, for focus, by the ring.

literals.reason: No vertical padding token exists. It is derived from 40px height minus 20px line height, split evenly.
No Button focus-radius token exists. The value is button.radius (6px) plus button.focus.offset (2px). Input has input.focus.radius; Button does not.
Figma stroke alignment is a geometry property, not a token. It is required so the ring does not reduce the 40px surface.
Font family is a Figma text property; no font-family token exists in v0.1.
There is no button.ghost.background token. Ghost intentionally lets the page surface show through.

literals.value: content width at the demo label (76px for 'Button')
literals.reason: No width or min-width token exists. Production width may stretch through layout, but height and radius must not change.

properties.name: Variant
properties.description: Visual emphasis. Exactly one value per instance. Primary is the strongest action, Secondary is a quieter alternative, Ghost is the lowest-emphasis action.

production.notes: Lowercase mapping only. There is no danger, success, link, outline or ghost-inverse value.

properties.name: State
properties.description: One of five mutually exclusive design states. The state is selected by interaction in production, not supplied by the caller.

production.notes: Do not expose a state prop. Surface state is disabled > active > hover > default; the focus ring is an additive keyboard-focus overlay unless disabled. State=Focus in Figma shows the variant's Default surface plus the ring.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: The visible action text. The Figma default 'Button' is demo content, not production copy.

production.notes: Must be non-empty. Use a verb-led, specific label. The label is the accessible name; do not add an icon-only mode.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Maps to State=Disabled. Renders the native disabled attribute, removes the button from tab order and suppresses hover, active and focus treatments.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Do not use aria-disabled alone. Do not use disabled as a validation strategy.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Native button type. Default to 'button' so a button placed inside a form does not submit accidentally; set 'submit' explicitly for form submission.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: The HTML default is 'submit'; the contract requires an explicit safe default.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Click handler supplied by the application. It must not fire when disabled.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Prefer form onSubmit for submit actions so keyboard and assistive-technology activation follow native form behaviour.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Layout-only escape hatch for external spacing, flex alignment and width.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: Must not be used to change colour, typography, radius, height, border or focus treatment.

codeOnlyProperties.type: ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> excluding children, disabled and type
codeOnlyProperties.description: Standard attributes such as id, name, value, form, autoFocus and aria-* pass through.
codeOnlyProperties.notes: aria-pressed, aria-expanded and other toggle semantics are not supported because no toggle contract exists.

codeOnlyProperties.description: Controls the size variant (sm, md, lg) in component adapter.
Applies loading state and sets aria-busy="true".

variants.name: Primary/Default
variants.notes: 76x40 at the demo label 'Button'. The strongest enabled resting action.

variants.name: Primary/Hover
variants.notes: Pointer-over surface. The label contrast remains 6.70:1.

variants.name: Primary/Active
variants.notes: Pointer-down surface. The label contrast remains 8.72:1.

variants.name: Primary/Focus
variants.notes: 80x44: the Default surface wrapped by a 2px ring at 2px offset. This is keyboard focus, not a persistent state.

variants.name: Primary/Disabled
variants.notes: Flat muted fill and muted text. Contrast is exempt because the control is inactive.

variants.name: Secondary/Default
variants.notes: Quiet filled alternative to Primary. No border is used.

variants.name: Secondary/Hover
variants.notes: One neutral step darker than Secondary/Default.

variants.name: Secondary/Active
variants.notes: Pointer-down surface, one further neutral step darker.

variants.name: Secondary/Focus
variants.notes: 80x44: Secondary/Default surface plus the focus ring.

variants.name: Secondary/Disabled
variants.notes: Shares the disabled fill and text with Primary/Disabled.

variants.name: Ghost/Default
variants.notes: Transparent background; the page surface shows through. Contrast is measured against color.surface.default.

variants.name: Ghost/Hover
variants.notes: A subtle neutral fill appears on hover.

variants.name: Ghost/Active
variants.notes: A stronger neutral fill appears while pressed.

variants.name: Ghost/Focus
variants.notes: 80x44: transparent surface plus the focus ring. No default Ghost background token exists.

variants.name: Ghost/Disabled
variants.notes: Transparent background with disabled text. Contrast is 2.56:1 on white and is exempt because the control is inactive.

validCombinations.result: Primary default surface, foreground and focus ring.
Shared disabled surface and foreground; no interaction.
Secondary default surface, foreground and focus ring.
Shared disabled surface and foreground; no interaction.
Ghost hover surface and ghost foreground.
Ghost active surface and ghost foreground.
Transparent surface, ghost foreground and focus ring.
Transparent surface and disabled foreground; no interaction.
Not modelled in Figma. The flat State axis allows only one State value; do not create a combined variant.
Not modelled in Figma. The flat State axis allows only one State value; do not create a combined variant.
Disabled is a single State; disabled wins and suppresses hover, active and focus treatments.

precedence: Figma: exactly one Variant and exactly one State per instance. The 15 variants are the complete design matrix.
Figma: State values are mutually exclusive. Focus is a State, not a boolean, because the Button focus variant wraps the surface in a ring frame.
Figma: State=Focus renders the variant's Default surface plus the ring. It does not represent a hovered or pressed surface.
Production surface: disabled > active > hover > default.
Production focus: the ring is an additive keyboard-focus overlay, suppressed when disabled. This is a design-to-code translation for CSS pseudo-classes, not an additional Figma variant.
Production: keyboard focus must remain visible even when the pointer is also over the control; never suppress the ring to preserve a hover visual.
conflicts: Focus + Hover is not modelled in Figma. Do not claim a Hover+Focus variant exists and do not create one in this contract version.
Focus + Active is not modelled in Figma. Do not claim an Active+Focus variant exists.
Disabled overrides hover, active and focus. A disabled control must not show a ring or respond to pointer states.
Do not use the Focus variant to represent a button that is permanently highlighted; focus is an interaction state.
Do not approximate Hover+Focus by stacking two Figma variants; the set has no such combination.
notes: State names are design metadata. They do not map to ARIA attributes; native button behaviour and the disabled attribute carry the semantics.
Hover and Focus are not independent axes. There is no combined Hover+Focus state and no way to select one; the ring is an indicator, not a second state axis.
Adding a sixth State or a combined state requires a new Figma build and a new contract version.
Button has one size. There is no small, large, compact or icon-only axis.
The focus ring must remain visible at every supported surface; it is not decorative.

tokens.rule: Component code and Figma instances consume only button.* component tokens. Colour tokens alias Semantic roles; geometry and typography tokens alias Primitives because no semantic geometry layer exists. Never consume a primitive or Semantic token directly, and never hardcode a hex or px value that a token already covers.

dependencies.name: button.disabled.background
dependencies.role: Disabled surface for Primary and Secondary

stateMapping.notes: Ring width and offset come from button.focus.width and button.focus.offset.
Ring width and offset come from button.focus.width and button.focus.offset.
Transparent surface; ring width and offset come from button.focus.width and button.focus.offset.
Transparent surface; the disabled label is the only visual change.

forbidden: Do not consume color.action.*, color.content.*, color.border.*, blue.*, neutral.* or any other primitive or Semantic token directly in Button code.
Do not hardcode #2563EB, #1D4ED8, #1E40AF, #FFFFFF, #F4F4F5, #E4E4E7, #D4D4D8, #18181B or #A1A1AA when a button.* token exists.
Do not introduce a button.danger.*, button.success.*, button.ghost.background or button.focus.radius token without a token-source change and contract version.
Do not override tokens per instance; theme overrides belong at the token layer and require contrast revalidation.
Do not use the Input focus tokens for Button; Button has its own button.focus.* tokens.

design.requirement: Every variant is 40px high, above the 24px minimum target, and remains comfortably wider than 40px at its default label.
design.verification: Measure the rendered height and bounding box for all 15 variants at 100% zoom.

design.requirement: Focus is a 2px ring at a 2px offset, drawn OUTSIDE, with a 3:1 minimum against the adjacent surface.
design.verification: Inspect the Focus variant geometry and measure button.focus.color against default, canvas, subtle, muted and inverse.

design.requirement: Enabled label text meets 4.5:1 against its own surface in Default, Hover, Active and Focus.
design.verification: Use the contrast matrix in this contract or recompute from resolved token values.

design.requirement: Disabled text is deliberately low contrast (2.02:1 for Primary/Secondary, 2.56:1 for Ghost on white) and is exempt under WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 because the control is inactive.
design.verification: Confirm the disabled treatment is recorded as exempt, not reported as a passing contrast pair.

design.requirement: Hover, active and focus are not signalled by colour alone: surface fill changes for hover/active and a ring appears for focus. Disabled changes fill and text and removes interaction.
design.verification: Compare grayscale renders and confirm the focus ring remains visible without colour perception.

design.requirement: Variant and State names are design metadata. They must not be emitted as ARIA attributes or accessible names.
design.verification: Inspect the accessibility tree: the only name is the label; the only state is native disabled/focus.

production.requirement: Render a native <button> element. Do not use a div or span with role='button'.
The visible label is the accessible name and must be non-empty. There is no icon-only mode and no aria-label-only mode.
production.verification: Assert the computed accessible name equals the label text.

production.requirement: Enter and Space activate the button through native behaviour. The button is reachable by Tab in DOM order. Disabled removes it from the tab order.
production.verification: Keyboard-only test in Chromium, Firefox and Safari.

production.requirement: Show the 2px ring for :focus-visible. Never set outline: none without an equivalent visible replacement. The ring must not be clipped by overflow or a parent container.
production.verification: Tab to every variant and inspect the ring at 100% and 200% zoom.

production.requirement: Use the native disabled attribute. Do not use aria-disabled alone; do not leave a disabled-looking button focusable and clickable.
production.verification: Assert disabled is present, the button is not focusable, and click/submit handlers do not fire.

production.requirement: Keep the rendered height at 40px. Do not compress the button below 24px in dense layouts.
production.verification: Measure the bounding box after layout in every composition.

production.requirement: There is no loading state. When work is asynchronous, announce status in a separate live region and guard duplicate submission; do not silently disable the button as the only feedback.
production.verification: Simulate a slow submit and confirm an assistive-technology announcement plus duplicate-submit protection.

production.requirement: In forced-colors mode, the button must retain a visible boundary or focus indicator using system colours. The contract does not model forced colours with tokens.
production.verification: Test Windows High Contrast / forced-colors emulation in Chromium and Firefox.

production.requirement: Labels may grow or wrap in translation. Do not fix the width or truncate the only accessible name.
production.verification: Test a long translated label and 200% text zoom without clipping the label or ring.

production.requirement: A button must not change the current location. Navigation belongs to a link.
production.verification: Code review and DOM assertion that the control is a button, not an anchor.

contrast.notes: neutral.900 on white; Ghost is transparent.
Inactive control; WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 exclude disabled controls.
Inactive control; transparent Ghost on white. Exempt.
2px ring at 2px offset. All measured surfaces meet the 3:1 non-text minimum, including inverse.
Unsupported. Ghost is transparent, so neutral.900 text sits on neutral.900. Do not place Ghost on inverse.

allowed: Change the label copy and localise it; keep it verb-led and specific.
Choose Primary, Secondary or Ghost according to action hierarchy.
Stretch the button through its container for layout; keep height, radius, padding and typography unchanged.
Pass standard native button attributes such as id, name, value, form and aria-*.
Supply an onClick handler for actions and type='submit' for form submission.
Override component token values at the theme layer, provided the three-layer alias chain is preserved and every contrast pair is revalidated.
Wrap the button in application layout that does not clip its focus ring.
forbidden: Hardcoding colours, radii, heights, padding, font sizes or weights.
Adding a danger, success, link, outline, loading, icon-only or full-width variant.
Changing the 40px height, 6px radius, 16px horizontal padding, 14/20 label or 500 weight.
Removing or restyling the focus ring.
Using aria-disabled without the native disabled attribute, or leaving a disabled-looking control interactive.
Using role='button' on a non-button element.
Placing two Primary buttons in the same decision group.
Using aria-pressed, aria-expanded or other toggle semantics without a toggle contract.
Placing Ghost on an inverse surface.
Applying a one-off visual override to an instance instead of correcting the token or contract.
themeOverrides: Consumers may remap semantic action and focus roles so button.primary.background, button.secondary.background and button.focus.color resolve to a brand palette.
Every override must preserve the component-token alias chain and be revalidated for text contrast, disabled exemption, focus-ring contrast and hover/active differentiation.
Do not add new component-token names in a theme; a missing role requires a token-source change and a new contract version.
Light theme is the only implemented theme. Dark mode is not available and must not be simulated by inverting values.

canonical: Use one Primary action per form, dialog or decision group and place it last in the reading order when it advances the task.
Pair Primary with Secondary for a cancel or back action; keep the secondary action visually quieter.
Use Ghost for low-emphasis actions in toolbars, rows and dense panels where a filled surface would compete with content.
Keep the label verb-led and specific: 'Review transfer', 'Save changes', 'Cancel'.
Preserve DOM order that matches the visual order; do not use CSS order to reverse a primary and secondary action.
Give the button a stable width or allow it to grow with translated copy; never clip the label or ring.
forbidden: Two Primary buttons for the same decision.
A button nested inside another button or inside a link.
Using Button for navigation; use a link.
Using Button as an input adornment, clear button or password reveal; there is no icon system.
A destructive action rendered by overriding Primary with red.
A disabled submit button used instead of showing validation errors.
Placing Ghost on inverse or dark surfaces.

invalidConfigurations.why: State is derived from interaction in production. A caller-supplied state lets an application fake hover, active or focus and breaks the single source of truth.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Render <Button variant="primary" label="Continue" /> and let :hover, :active, :focus-visible and disabled drive the visual state.

invalidConfigurations.why: The Button component has a flat five-value State axis. No combined state exists and none is approved.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Keep the 15-variant matrix. In production, the focus ring overlays the current surface; do not create a combined Figma variant.

invalidConfigurations.why: There is no danger variant, danger token or destructive contrast guarantee.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Do not implement destructive styling in v0.1. Request a destructive variant through the design-system process.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: <Button loading label="Saving" /> with an inline spinner.
invalidConfigurations.why: No loading state, spinner, progress token or async contract exists.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Keep the label stable, guard duplicate submission, and announce async status in a separate live region.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: A square button containing only a trash icon with aria-label.
invalidConfigurations.why: There is no icon system or icon-only contract, and the visible label is the required accessible name.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Use a text label such as 'Delete'. Wait for an icon-button contract before adding icons.

invalidConfigurations.why: Hardcoded values bypass the button.* token chain and will not follow theme overrides.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Use variant='primary' and the button.primary.* component tokens.

invalidConfigurations.why: Ghost text is neutral.900 on a neutral.900 surface in the default theme: 1.00:1.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Do not place Ghost on inverse. Use a supported light surface or obtain a new inverse-surface contract.

invalidConfigurations.why: A button that navigates breaks link semantics, middle-click, open-in-new-tab and expected assistive-technology behaviour.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Render a semantic link styled consistently, or wait for a Link component.

invalidConfigurations.why: The control remains focusable and clickable unless the handler is guarded; the visual state is not the native disabled state.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Use disabled; if a focusable disabled control is ever required, that needs a separate contract.

invalidConfigurations.why: Keyboard users lose the only focus indicator. The design requires a 2px ring at 2px offset.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Render :focus-visible with button.focus.color, button.focus.width and button.focus.offset; never remove the indicator without an equivalent.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: A 32px-high button with a 4px radius and 8px horizontal padding.
invalidConfigurations.why: Only one size exists: 40px high, 6px radius, 16px horizontal padding. A smaller button would also risk the 24px target minimum.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Keep the token geometry. If a compact size is required, add a size contract and tokens first.

invalidConfigurations.configuration: Two Primary buttons side by side: 'Save' and 'Save and close'.
invalidConfigurations.why: Competing primary actions remove hierarchy and increase decision error in financial flows.
invalidConfigurations.correct: Choose one Primary action and express the alternative as Secondary or Ghost, or combine the actions into one clear flow.

visual.given: The Button component is rendered at 100% zoom on a supported light surface.
visual.when: Each of the 15 Variant x State combinations is captured.
visual.then: Every surface, foreground and ring resolves to the token values in this contract; no hex or px literal appears in the render tree.

visual.given: A Button with the demo label 'Button'.
visual.then: Height is 40px, radius is 6px, horizontal padding is 16px, label is 14/20 at weight 500, and the Focus state is 44px high including the 2px ring at 2px offset.

visual.given: Each variant in the Focus state.
visual.then: The ring is 2px wide, offset 2px, drawn OUTSIDE, has an 8px outer radius, and the inner surface remains 40px high.

visual.given: Each variant in the Disabled state.
visual.when: The surface and label are compared with the enabled states.
visual.then: Primary and Secondary use the shared muted fill and muted label; Ghost stays transparent and uses the muted label; no hover, active or ring treatment is visible.
The button has no fill of its own; the page surface shows through and only the label (and ring, for focus) is visible.

behaviour.given: An enabled Button with an onClick handler.
An enabled Button reached by Tab.
behaviour.then: The button activates exactly as a native button and the focus ring is visible.

behaviour.when: The user clicks, presses Enter or presses Space, and tabs through the page.
behaviour.then: No handler fires, the button is skipped in the tab order, and no hover, active or ring treatment appears.

behaviour.given: A Button with type='submit' inside a form.
behaviour.when: The button is activated by pointer or keyboard.
behaviour.then: The form submits once. A Button with type='button' does not submit.

behaviour.given: A Button rendered with a label.
behaviour.when: The label is changed through the supported prop.
behaviour.then: The visible text updates, the accessible name updates, and the variant tokens remain bound.

behaviour.when: The pointer enters and then presses.
behaviour.then: The surface changes from default to hover to active using the matching button.* tokens, and returns to default on leave or release.

accessibility.then: The role is button, the accessible name equals the visible label, and no State or Variant text is announced.

accessibility.given: All enabled variants and the focus ring.
accessibility.when: Contrast is measured from resolved values.
accessibility.then: Every enabled text pair is at least 4.5:1 and the focus ring is at least 3:1 on every supported surface.

accessibility.given: A keyboard user tabbing through a page.
accessibility.then: The 2px ring is visible, not clipped, and persists while the pointer also hovers.

accessibility.when: The accessibility tree and tab order are inspected.
accessibility.then: The native disabled state is exposed and the control is not focusable or activatable.

accessibility.when: The button is rendered in default, focus and disabled states.
accessibility.then: A visible boundary or focus indicator remains; the control does not disappear into the background.

accessibility.given: 200% text zoom and a long translated label.
accessibility.then: The label remains readable and is not clipped; the height may grow rather than cutting text.

tokens.given: The Button implementation and its resolved styles.
tokens.when: Every colour, dimension and font-weight reference is audited.
tokens.then: Every reference is a button.* component token; there are zero primitive or Semantic references and zero hardcoded values covered by a token.

tokens.when: The dependency list is compared with tokens/tokens.json.
tokens.then: All 22 button.* dependencies exist, resolve to the stated values, and map to the stated --fc-* CSS variables.

tokens.when: Each surface, foreground and ring is checked against stateMapping.
tokens.then: Every visual property resolves to the mapped token and no variant uses a token from the wrong state.

tokens.when: Searching for button.danger, button.success, button.loading, button.ghost.background, button.focus.radius or a size variant.
tokens.then: No such token or API exists in the implementation.

regression.given: A baseline snapshot of all 15 variants.
regression.then: Every variant is pixel-compared; any change to surface, text, geometry or ring is reviewed and explained.

regression.given: The protected token source, validator and generated CSS.
regression.then: tokens/tokens.json, tokens/check.mjs and tokens/dist/tokens.css are byte-identical to the baseline hashes.
The set still has 15 variants, 3 properties, the same variant IDs, and no duplicate or combined state.

regression.when: The browser back/forward and open-in-new-tab behaviour is tested.
regression.then: Buttons do not create history entries or new tabs; only links do.

limitations.limitation: Button uses a flat five-value State axis. Focus cannot be combined with Hover or Active in Figma.
limitations.impact: There is no approved combined visual reference for a focused button that is also hovered or pressed.
limitations.mitigation: Production keeps the ring as an additive keyboard-focus overlay. Do not create combined Figma variants; request a new design if the combined visual matters.

limitations.limitation: State=Focus renders the variant's Default surface, not the Hover or Active surface.
limitations.impact: A focused-and-hovered button has no single Figma reference.
limitations.mitigation: Treat the ring as the required focus signal and let the surface follow the pointer state; record any visual decision in the implementation tests.

limitations.limitation: There is no button.focus.radius token. The 8px outer ring radius is a literal derived from 6px + 2px.
limitations.impact: A theme that changes button.radius or button.focus.offset must also update the literal.
limitations.mitigation: Add a dedicated Button focus-radius token in a future token change; until then, assert the 8px arithmetic in visual tests.

limitations.limitation: There is no vertical padding token; 10px is derived from the 40px height and 20px line height.
limitations.impact: Changing the line height or height without recalculating padding can break vertical centring.
limitations.mitigation: Keep the height and line height token-bound and assert vertical centring in visual tests.

limitations.limitation: IBM Plex Sans is a Figma text property, not a token.
limitations.impact: Production font loading and fallback are not governed by the token source.
limitations.mitigation: The application owns font loading and must verify the rendered metrics; a font-family token is future work.

limitations.limitation: There is no icon system, icon slot or icon-only variant.
limitations.impact: Buttons cannot carry leading/trailing icons or stand alone as icon actions.
limitations.mitigation: Use text-only labels. Wait for an icon and icon-button contract.

limitations.limitation: There is no loading, spinner or progress state.
limitations.impact: Async actions have no built-in busy visual.
limitations.mitigation: Keep the label stable, guard duplicate submission, and announce status in a separate live region.

limitations.limitation: There is no danger, critical or destructive variant.
limitations.impact: Destructive actions cannot be styled within the contract.
limitations.mitigation: Do not override Primary with red. Request a destructive variant through the design-system process.

limitations.limitation: There is no pressed, selected or toggle state.
limitations.impact: Button cannot represent on/off or selected controls.
limitations.mitigation: Use a future Toggle, Switch or Segmented Control component.

limitations.limitation: Inverse surfaces are not a supported Button context. Ghost fails at 1.00:1; Primary and Secondary have no inverse-specific tokens.
limitations.impact: The component cannot be declared safe on dark or inverse surfaces.
limitations.mitigation: Stay on supported light surfaces. A future inverse contract must add surface-specific tokens and revalidate every state.

limitations.limitation: Disabled text is 2.02:1 for Primary/Secondary and 2.56:1 for Ghost on white. It is exempt, not accessible.
limitations.impact: Disabled controls are difficult to read for low-vision users.
limitations.mitigation: Use disabled sparingly and always explain why the action is unavailable in surrounding text. The exemption is recorded, not hidden.

limitations.limitation: Width is content-driven; the demo label is 76px wide and no width or min-width token exists.
limitations.impact: Translated labels change width and can disrupt dense layouts.
limitations.mitigation: Allow growth and test long labels; use layout constraints rather than fixed widths.

limitations.limitation: There is only one size: 40px high with 14/20 text.
limitations.impact: Compact and large contexts cannot be served by a size variant.
limitations.mitigation: Do not compress the button below 24px. A size contract is future work.

limitations.limitation: Figma State is a design axis; it is not a runtime prop, DOM attribute or ARIA state.
limitations.impact: Copying the Figma property directly into an API would let callers fake interaction states.
limitations.mitigation: Derive state from :hover, :active, :focus-visible and disabled; do not expose a state prop.

limitations.impact: No dark values exist for any Button token, including focus and disabled.
limitations.mitigation: Ship light theme only. Do not invert values to simulate dark mode.

readOrder: Read this contract.json completely before writing Button code.
Read components/button/README.md for the human explanation, native HTML/CSS mapping and examples.
Read components/IMPLEMENTATION.md and components/button/button.css plus button.html for the actual native implementation. Contract-level props are not runtime exports.
Read tokens/tokens.json or tokens/dist/tokens.css for the canonical token names and resolved values.
Read docs/foundation/principles.md for accessibility and semantic-token rules.
Read components/examples/financial-form.md only after the Button contract is understood; it is illustrative, not a production feature.
rules: Use only variant='primary' | 'secondary' | 'ghost'. Do not invent danger, success, link, outline, loading, icon-only, full-width or size variants.
Use only the length, width, radius, padding, typography and focus tokens listed in this contract.
Render a native button. Derive state from interaction; do not accept a state prop.
Use the native disabled attribute. Do not substitute aria-disabled alone.
Keep the visible label as the accessible name. Do not add an icon-only mode.
Never remove the focus ring. Use :focus-visible and keep the ring unclipped.
Do not use a button for navigation. Use a link.
Do not implement loading, progress or async feedback inside the button.
Do not place Ghost on inverse or dark surfaces.

Treat the native class/attribute API as canonical: .fc-button plus the variant class, text content as the label, native disabled, explicit type, and browser pseudo-classes for interaction states. Do not require a JavaScript runtime or React adapter.
Use button.ghost.foreground for every Ghost label, including Ghost/Focus. The previous color/content/link binding was corrected in Stage 5C-1 and verified.
Do not modify tokens/tokens.json, tokens/check.mjs or tokens/dist/tokens.css to make an implementation easier. If a role is missing, stop and report it.
uncertaintyPolicy: If the requested action is destructive, loading, toggle-like, icon-only or navigation, stop and report that the capability is not in the contract. Do not approximate it with Primary.
If the requested surface is inverse or dark, stop and report that the surface is unsupported.
If a required token is missing, report the missing role and the token chain it would need; do not hardcode a value.
If the desired label or action hierarchy is unclear, ask for the action's intent rather than choosing a variant silently.
If a design shows a Hover+Focus or Active+Focus combined state, flag it as an open question; do not create a combined variant.
If the implementation target is not specified, ask before choosing a framework, package path or styling approach.
definitionOfDone: All 15 visual combinations render from button.* tokens with no primitive, Semantic or hardcoded values covered by a token.
Click, keyboard activation, form submission, disabled behaviour and label updates pass.
The focus ring is visible and unclipped at 100% and 200% zoom, including while hovered.
Accessible name, role, disabled semantics and target size pass an accessibility audit.
The 22 token dependencies resolve to the values in this contract and match the generated CSS variables.
No unsupported variant, state, icon, loading behaviour, navigation or inverse usage is present.
The illustrative composition example, if used, is adapted rather than copied as production code.

valid.title: Primary form submission
valid.explanation: One primary action, explicit submit type, visible verb-led label. The application owns validation and submission.

valid.title: Secondary cancel action
valid.explanation: A quieter alternative next to the primary action. type='button' prevents accidental form submission.

valid.title: Ghost toolbar action
valid.explanation: Low emphasis on a supported light surface. Ghost is not used on inverse or dark backgrounds.

valid.title: Genuinely unavailable action
valid.explanation: Disabled is used only when the action is truly unavailable, with the reason explained outside the button.

invalid.title: Invented danger variant
invalid.explanation: No danger variant or danger token exists. This also implies destructive styling without a contrast contract.

invalid.title: Caller-supplied interaction state
invalid.explanation: State is derived from the interaction. Exposing it lets an application fake hover, active or focus.

invalid.title: Icon-only button
invalid.explanation: There is no icon system or icon-only variant, and the visible label is the required accessible name.

invalid.title: Hardcoded visual override
invalid.explanation: Bypasses the button.* token chain, changes the approved height and breaks themeability.

invalid.title: Ghost on inverse
invalid.explanation: Ghost text is neutral.900 on a neutral.900 surface in the default theme: 1.00:1. Inverse is unsupported.

invalid.title: Button used for navigation
invalid.explanation: Navigation must use a link so history, open-in-new-tab and assistive-technology expectations are preserved.

invalid.title: Fake loading state
invalid.explanation: There is no loading contract. A changed label and disabled state are not sufficient async feedback.

invalid.title: aria-disabled only
invalid.explanation: The control remains focusable and clickable. Use the native disabled attribute.
